tool.name: DataServicePillagerTool

param.name: service_endpoint
param.dialogReference:
Arrrr! Enter ye service url here.

F'r a single layer, make sure ye has the layer id number. Else, it grabs all the sublayers!

Example:

Single layer: http://www.myserver.com/arcgis/rest/services/Service/MapServer/0

All layers: http://www.myserver.com/arcgis/rest/services/Service/MapServer

param.name: output_workspace
param.dialogReference: This be the spot where ye want to stash yer loot, savvy? A filegeodatabase be the finest treasure chest, but a sturdy ol' folder or yer SDE will do in a pinch, it's yer call. Mind ye, if it's a folder or filegeodatabase ye choose, we'll be makin' it anew for yer purposes!

param.name: max_tries
param.dialogReference: If the scallywag query fails to hoist anchor, this be how many times we'll be making another go of it, cos we's persistent like.

param.name: sleep_time
param.dialogReference: This be the number o' seconds we slumber afore we try again.

param.name: strict_mode
param.dialogReference: Yer service be needin' to hoist the JSON flag, so keep that at True, savvy? But if ye fancy temptin' the Kraken, try False at yer own peril.

param.name: username
param.dialogReference: Sail ho! If ye knows someone on the inside, put their name here to git up to the gate safely.

param.name: password
param.dialogReference: No quarter! Enter ye secret password to get past the scurvy guards.

param.name: referring_domain
param.dialogReference:
Not needed for *.arcgis.com services, cos we knows that one.

If ye username or password is fer a different url as yer service url, enter it here.

Fer example, if yer federated server (myserver.com/server) makes yer log in through portal (myserver.com/portal) then that's yer referring domain.

param.name: existing_token
param.dialogReference: If ye have a shiny token fer getting past the guards, enter it here. Overrides yer password and username, so make sure it works fer long enough.

param.name: query_str
param.dialogReference:
Fer being selective-like, but yer takes yer chances here. A wise old sea dog gave me this advice:

This must be a well-formed and valid SQL query used to limit the data, entered without encoding! It is suggested you generate a SQL query suitable for the data from the REST endpoint "Where" box and paste it in. It will be automatically parsed for the url query. An example of a valid query might be ST_ABBREV IN ('WA', 'OR')

The SQL string will be added to the where clause used to select and download the data. As the Pillager also does an OID where clause, there may be cases where the SQL you pass in causes nothing to be returned. You should always check that the SQL is correct.

param.name: enforce_ssl_verification
param.dialogReference: We don't need no stinkin' security validation, but if yer do, check the box.

param.name: ca_bundle_path
param.dialogReference: If yer insist on validation, maybe yer has a custom CA Bundle file wot you wants used instead of yer default OS certs.

param.name: create_empty_schema
param.displayname: Create Empty Schema If No Features
param.dialogReference: If ye choose this path, we creates an output even if it's empty.

param.name: overwrite_output
param.dialogReference: Takin' no care to preserve what ye might already have.

param.name: preserve_global_ids
param.dialogReference: Flies the flag (arcpy.env) to preserve globalid values, fer extra value

param.name: write_service_info
param.dialogReference: Yar, we can grab some metadata and stuff about each layer, writin' it ter file. Or not.

param.name: include_attachments
param.dialogReference: When ye want all the goodies, but beware, can take longer and takes up a lot of space (we recommends you select the cleanup option)

param.name: clean_up_temp_attachments_data
param.dialogReference: We deletes the temporary stuff as we go, so yer storage can keeps up

tool.summary:
Yaar!

Like a pirate on the seven seas, this tool will rampantly pillage data from an ArcGIS Service. Handles sub layers in a service, or just one.

If the service is secured, you need a username and password (or a valid token).

The referring domain is the location for the security token service, and should be added when this differs from the root url of the service (e.g. federated Enterprise services), and only if the service needs a username and password.

You can enter a token if you have one. Do not enter a username and password if you have a valid token!

Strict mode will check that the service supports JSON. Turn it off if you prefer to take yer chances...

The pillager will generate service info text files in yer output folder by default. It can also download attachments and add them to the fgdb/sde output. Beware that these can take up a lot of space so it is recommended to clean up the temporary files for this, unless you want a file copy.
